content.title: Links and Buttons Must Say What They Do
content.hook: A control label is part of the interface contract. “Click here” tells the user almost nothing. “View billing history” explains the destination. “Save changes” describes the action.

content.question: A list of account links contains one generic label: “Learn more”. Which replacement is more useful when the destination is a security guide?

feedback.correct: Useful labels make sense on their own and tell the user what will happen or where the link goes.
feedback.incorrect: Useful labels make sense on their own and tell the user what will happen or where the link goes.

content.title: Specific navigation labels
content.text: ```html Read the account security guide View billing history ```

content.question: A control opens and changes the current interface without navigating to a new resource. Which is the stronger semantic choice?

feedback.correct: Buttons represent actions. Links represent navigation.
feedback.incorrect: Buttons represent actions. Links represent navigation.

content.title: Context without guesswork
content.text: A user should not have to remember what a vague label means. Prefer labels that remain understandable when the nearby paragraph is not read first.

activities.title: Tiny lab
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt: Take three controls from a page you know: one navigation control and two actions. Rewrite their labels so each one can be understood without “click here”, “more”, or “go”.
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.
content.sampleResponse: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.

feedback.correct: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.
feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

feedback.correct: “Continue” can be useful in some contexts, but a specific label gives a clearer promise about the result.
feedback.incorrect: “Continue” can be useful in some contexts, but a specific label gives a clearer promise about the result.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Mental model: Labels are promises. Make the promise specific.
Senior habit: Read controls out of context. If you cannot predict the result, the label is probably too vague.
